title: SAP Weighs Cutting at Least 10,000 Jobs in AI-First Restructuring
yt_title: SAP May Cut 10,000+ Jobs in AI-First Overhaul | IT News · AI News
yt_description:
SAP, Europe's biggest software company, is weighing at least 10,000 job cuts, more than 9% of its workforce, as CEO Christian Klein pushes an AI-first strategy, Bloomberg reports. SAP has not confirmed the plan, and its shares rose about 2% after the report.

script: Welcome to IT News, AI News! Big news from Germany: software giant SAP may cut at least ten thousand jobs. That's according to Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter. The reason? Artificial intelligence. SAP wants to become an AI-first company. Ten thousand jobs is at least nine percent of SAP's workforce of more than one hundred ten thousand people. Every single department has reportedly been asked to find possible cuts. Product, engineering and sales are said to be in the spotlight. CEO Christian Klein wants AI tools built right into SAP's business apps. SAP says its AI assistant, Joule, already boosts productivity by about twenty percent in finance, HR and purchasing. And its developers wrote about seventy percent more code this year. Robots typing faster than ever! SAP did not confirm the plan. It says it continuously reviews its organization to stay aligned with its strategy. Investors? They seemed to like it. SAP shares rose about two percent after the report. Feeling deja vu? In twenty twenty-four, SAP restructured around ten thousand roles, for about three billion euros. Back then, total headcount stayed roughly flat, because SAP kept hiring in AI and other growth areas. In Germany, a works council deal guarantees jobs until twenty twenty-eight, so staff there must be offered other roles or retraining. The final number could still change after labor talks. SAP usually announces big restructurings in late January. AI is reshaping software, and the people who build it. Read the full story on itnewsainews dot xpigeon dot net!
